answer_sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT
    c.country_code,
    SUM(s.net_amount) AS net_revenue,
    COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_key) AS buyers
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS s
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
    ON s.customer_key = c.customer_key
  GROUP BY
    c.country_code
), reg AS (
  SELECT
    country_code,
    COUNT(*) AS on_register
  FROM contoso_served.dim_customer
  GROUP BY
    country_code
)
SELECT
  co.country_name AS country,
  ROUND(rev.net_revenue / rev.buyers, 2) AS revenue_per_buyer,
  ROUND(rev.net_revenue / reg.on_register, 2) AS revenue_per_registered_customer
FROM rev
JOIN reg
  ON rev.country_code = reg.country_code
JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS co
  ON rev.country_code = co.country_code
ORDER BY
  rev.net_revenue / rev.buyers DESC

body.value: For each of the 8 countries Contoso's customers live in, the average amount one customer there has spent with Contoso over the entire ten years on record, after discount — stated twice because the divisor is genuinely ambiguous. Under Reading A a row is the average lifetime spend of a person who bought at least once; under Reading B it is the same money spread across every name on that country's register, so it reads as revenue per registered name and comes out roughly half as large. Each row stands for one country, with internet purchases counted to the buyer's home country rather than to a channel with no country. WHAT I DID NOT INCLUDE: no period restriction (all ten years, not this year or the last twelve months), no channel restriction (the web shop is in), no gross figure (these are net), no per-order or per-line view (this is per PERSON), and no listing of individual customers (these are 8 country averages, not 52,189 customer rows).

value:
Which "per customer" do you mean — per person who actually bought, or per name on the customer register? Both are computed in full below; they differ by about half on every row, and no rule in this bundle chooses, so I am not picking for you.

READING A — per BUYER (each country's revenue ÷ the people there who bought at least once; 52,189 buyers):
United States 4,505.30 · Germany 4,437.83 · Canada 4,313.67 · Netherlands 3,877.17 · United Kingdom 3,738.77 · Italy 3,564.05 · France 3,350.77 · Australia 3,347.70

READING B — per REGISTERED CUSTOMER (the same revenue ÷ everyone on that country's register, including the 52,801 who never ordered; 104,990 people):
United States 2,475.76 · Germany 2,468.57 · Canada 2,298.69 · Netherlands 1,918.45 · United Kingdom 1,559.40 · France 1,368.05 · Australia 1,321.79 · Italy 1,303.61

WHAT YOUR CHOICE DOES NOT CHANGE: the winner and the whole top five, in the same order — United States, Germany, Canada, Netherlands, United Kingdom. It moves only places 6 to 8: Italy is 6th on A but LAST on B, because just 36.6% of registered Italians ever bought against 55.6% of Germans. France and Australia swap 7th and 8th.

TWO NEAR-TIES ON EITHER READING: the US lead over Germany is 1.5% on A and only 0.3% on B, so "highest" is near a dead heat. On A, France (3,350.77) and Australia (3,347.70) differ by 3.07 — 0.09% — so their 7th/8th order is not a real difference.

FIXED WHICHEVER YOU PICK: revenue is NET of discount, totalling 218,814,471.66 (gross is ~6.3% higher and reorders nothing); it covers all ten years on record, 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31, because no period was named; it includes the web shop's 86,790,054.13 as well as the physical shops; and each sale counts to where the BUYER lives, not where it was rung up. These are ten-year lifetime averages per person, not annual rates — a customer with forty orders counts once.

All 8 countries Contoso customers live in, computed over all 223,974 sales lines across the full order_date extent 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31. Nothing excluded: no channel predicate (both physical shops and the web shop — store.resolution.the_channel_is_the_location_sentinel is scoped `applies: subject` and so cannot reach a measure question, and the operator's 2026-10-18 ruling puts both channels in revenue), no date filter (order.default.an_unscoped_question_covers_all_time), no trading-state filter. The `--` sentinel is excluded per country.exclusion.sentinel_is_not_a_country but removes nothing, since no customer carries it. THE NUMERATOR IS IDENTICAL IN BOTH READINGS AND PROVEN COMPLETE: the 8 country totals sum to exactly 218,814,471.66, the declared all-channel net total, and their online share to exactly 86,790,054.13, the declared online total — so no sale is lost or double-counted. THE DIVISOR IS THE ONLY DIFFERENCE: Reading A divides by the 52,189 customers appearing on at least one sales line; Reading B divides by all 104,990 on the register, adding the 52,801 who never ordered. I restricted to neither — that is the open question I am returning.

WITH rev AS (

    c.country_code,
    SUM(s.net_amount) AS net_revenue,
    COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_key) AS buyers

  SELECT
    country_code,
    COUNT(*) AS on_register
  FROM contoso_served.dim_customer
  GROUP BY
    country_code

SELECT
  co.country_name,
  ROUND(rev.net_revenue, 2) AS net_revenue,
  rev.buyers,
  reg.on_register,
  ROUND(rev.net_revenue / rev.buyers, 2) AS per_buyer,
  ROUND(rev.net_revenue / reg.on_register, 2) AS per_registered,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY rev.net_revenue / rev.buyers DESC) AS rank_per_buyer,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY rev.net_revenue / reg.on_register DESC) AS rank_per_registered
FROM rev
JOIN reg
  ON rev.country_code = reg.country_code
JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS co
  ON rev.country_code = co.country_code
ORDER BY
  per_buyer DESC
